title: Two Weeks in Egypt: The Complete Itinerary
excerpt: A relaxed 14-day Egypt route: Cairo and Giza, a four-night Nile cruise, the Grand Egyptian Museum, Alexandria and the Red Sea, from about €1,529 per person for the package and tours.
body_html:
Prices, timetables and visiting details are a November 2026 snapshot. Check the linked official pages and your departure’s current inclusions and terms before booking.

Quick answer

In 2 weeks in Egypt you can cover the country's core without rushing: Cairo and Giza, the Grand Egyptian Museum, a day in Alexandria, a 4-night Nile cruise from Luxor to Aswan, and four Red Sea days in Hurghada. The relaxed build is the 9-day Egypt in Depth package plus three day tours: from about €1,529 per person for those parts, as listed in November 2026, before the hotel nights outside the package, the Cairo to Hurghada flight and international flights. If Abu Simbel is a must, swap the backbone for the 12-day Egypt End to End package, which includes it.

Check current UK government travel advice for Egypt before making your arrangements; advice can change.

Two weeks sounds generous for one country, until Egypt fills it. The classic squeeze: a week forces a choice between pyramids and temples, and 10 days cuts the Nile short. Done in the right order, 2 weeks in Egypt covers the full arc (Cairo and Giza, a 4-night Nile cruise, the Grand Egyptian Museum, Alexandria on the Mediterranean and a Red Sea finish) without a single forced march. Below is the whole 14-day route: one 9-day package, three day tours and four slow days, with prices and the honest trade-offs.

2 weeks in Egypt: the route at a glance

The best 2-week Egypt itinerary for a first visit runs north, then south, then to the sea: Cairo and Giza, four nights cruising from Luxor to Aswan, a flight back to Cairo for the Grand Egyptian Museum and a day trip to Alexandria, then four Red Sea days in Hurghada. The backbone is the 9-day Egypt in Depth Nile cruise and Cairo package, from €1,403 per person with its hotel nights, cruise, internal flights and sightseeing, in three comfort tiers (as listed in November 2026).

The route in one line: 3 nights in Cairo, 4 on the Nile, 3 back in Cairo, 3 in Hurghada, then fly home. The package and tours come to from about €1,529 per person (as listed in November 2026), before hotels outside the package and international flights.

The 14-day route, day by day

Days 1 to 9 run as the Egypt in Depth package sells them; it is a fixed product, so its days do not move. After that, two day tours from Cairo and a beach finish carry you to day 14.

Why the Grand Egyptian Museum gets its own day

Tutankhamun's collection is now at the Grand Egyptian Museum, not the Tahrir museum the package visits on day 3. Day 9 fixes that: the Secrets of the Grand Egyptian Museum tour runs about 3 hours with general admission included, from €48 per person (as listed in November 2026). Separately ticketed exhibitions inside the museum are not included. Because the package ends on day 9, you need your own Cairo hotel for that night and the next.

What about Abu Simbel?

Abu Simbel sits about 280 km south of Aswan, 3.5 to 4 hours each way by road, so it needs a full day and a night in Aswan. Egypt in Depth is a fixed package that flies you back to Cairo on day 8, and packages take no extensions, so Abu Simbel does not fit this route. Two honest options:

  • Choose Egypt End to End instead. The 12-day package includes Abu Simbel, a 3-night cruise from Aswan to Luxor and 3 nights in Hurghada, from €1,739 per person (as listed in November 2026). It drops Alexandria and has two long days: day 4 flies to Aswan and then drives to Abu Simbel and back, and day 8 covers both Luxor banks before the road to Hurghada, a very long day.
  • Build it from separate departures. The Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour, from €50 per person (as listed in November 2026), includes hotel pickup in Aswan. You can combine separate departures into one trip, but book your flights only after each date confirms.

Both Abu Simbel and Philae are monuments UNESCO helped save: Abu Simbel was cut apart and moved block by block between 1964 and 1968, and Philae was rebuilt on Agilkia Island in the 1970s, clear of the water behind the Aswan dams. For the sun-festival dates, see the guide to the Abu Simbel sun festival.

Where to add slow days

Add slow days at the two ends of the route: before the package starts and in Hurghada at the finish. The package middle is deliberately full and does not stretch.

  • Cairo, before the package. Arriving a day early, on your own hotel booking, gives you a jet-lag buffer and a slow Old Cairo or Khan el-Khalili morning before the guided days begin.
  • Alexandria, as an overnight. The day trip runs about 10 hours with roughly 3 hours of driving each way; staying over on your own booking halves the road time and adds the Corniche at sunset.
  • Luxor, from the cruise. A dawn hot-air balloon over the West Bank is listed as an optional extra on Egypt in Depth; it is not in the package price.
  • Hurghada, days 13 and 14. The easiest slow days on the route: no alarms, no coaches. A boat day like Orange Bay, or nothing at all.

What 2 weeks in Egypt costs

The fixed parts of this route cost from about €1,529 per person (as listed in November 2026) before international flights: the 9-day package plus the three day tours. Add the hotel nights outside the package, the Cairo to Hurghada flight and tipping on top.

Prices are fixed per traveller and do not change by season. Not included anywhere: international flights, travel insurance, drinks, the balloon, and tips. Baksheesh, the local custom of small gratuities, is expected and easiest budgeted as a daily amount. Most visitors also need a visa: check your passport and the current fee on the official portal, visa2egypt.gov.eg.

Who the 14-day route suits (and who it doesn't)

This route suits first-timers who want Cairo, the Nile and the sea in one trip, and anyone who wants Alexandria and the Grand Egyptian Museum without rushing them. Solo travellers can join too: on a package, a solo room or cabin is confirmed in the booking, so check it before you pay. It does not suit anyone who must see Abu Simbel; for that, Egypt End to End is the better backbone. And it does not suit anyone with fewer than about 12 days.

One road day is the honest cost of the extras: Alexandria means about 6 hours in a vehicle on day 10. If long drives ruin a holiday, cut Alexandria and keep a second slow day in Cairo.

How to book the route

Sawa Tours runs shared departures for the package and the three day tours on this route, with groups of four to eight travellers. Each part is a separate departure that confirms on its own, so check that each date is confirmed before you buy non-refundable flights. Start with Egypt in Depth or browse forming departures.

The verdict on two weeks in Egypt

Two weeks is Egypt's sweet spot: one package covers Cairo, Giza and the Nile; three day tours add the Grand Egyptian Museum, Alexandria and the reef; and four slow days in Hurghada give the trip room to breathe. If Abu Simbel matters more than Alexandria, take Egypt End to End instead.

About the author

Islam Hussein is an Egyptologist guide who has worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, and the founder of Sawa Tours. More about Sawa Tours.

faq.a: For a first visit: Cairo and Giza first, then the Nile, then the sea. Spend three days in Cairo, cruise four nights from Luxor to Aswan, fly back to Cairo for the Grand Egyptian Museum and a day trip to Alexandria, and finish with four Red Sea days in Hurghada. That is the 14-day route above: the 9-day Egypt in Depth package plus three day tours, from about €1,529 per person for those parts (as listed in November 2026).

faq.q: Is two weeks in Egypt too long?
faq.a: No. Two weeks is the shortest comfortable span for Cairo, the Nile and the Red Sea together. Under 10 days you must drop either the Red Sea or several temples. Outside the package days, this route has one long road day (Alexandria) and four unhurried beach days, so most travellers finish rested rather than wrecked.

faq.q: Can I add Abu Simbel to this route?
faq.a: Not to the package itself: Egypt in Depth is fixed and flies back to Cairo from Aswan. Choose the 12-day Egypt End to End package, which includes Abu Simbel, or combine separate departures and book flights only after each date confirms. The Aswan to Abu Simbel day tour is from €50 per person (as listed in November 2026), with hotel pickup in Aswan and 3.5 to 4 hours on the road each way.

faq.q: When is the best time for a two-week Egypt trip?
faq.a: October to April is the sweet stretch: Cairo, Luxor and Aswan turn fiercely hot in summer, and most days of this itinerary involve hours outdoors. The Red Sea is warm year-round, so Hurghada works in any month. Winter days are mild, but early mornings on the Nile can be chilly, so pack a layer.

faq.q: How much does a 2-week trip to Egypt cost?
faq.a: Budget from about €1,529 per person for the package and day tours before international flights (as listed in November 2026): Egypt in Depth from €1,403, plus €126 for the Grand Egyptian Museum, Alexandria and Orange Bay day tours (€48 + €47 + €31). Add the Cairo and Hurghada hotel nights outside the package, the Cairo to Hurghada flight, tips, drinks and travel insurance.

faq.q: Can I travel this route solo?
faq.a: Yes. Groups are never larger than eight, which makes solo travel sociable without feeling like a big-bus tour. On the package, a solo room or cabin is confirmed in the booking, so check what is confirmed before you pay.
